from.name: Microcom Networking Protocol error-control installed base

to.name: CCITT V.42 error-control ecosystem
to.revision: November 1988 generation and deployed compatible modems

property: V.42-era modem implementations preserve interoperability with the installed MNP error-control base while LAPM serves as the standardized V.42 error-control procedure.

date_or_range.notes: The relationship is best understood as compatibility/coexistence rather than a formal MNP-to-V.42 revision chain.

sources.supports: formal V.42 error-control standard lineage beginning in 1988
sources.notes: The normative 1988 text should be mined clause-by-clause for the exact alternate-procedure wording.

sources.locator: Telebit T3000/WorldBlazer modem manual, V.42/MNP error-control descriptions
sources.supports: deployed modems implementing LAPM while retaining MNP Classes 2-4 compatibility
sources.notes: Vendor implementation evidence demonstrates coexistence in products rather than proving how the standards committee arrived at the compatibility decision.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that MNP is a formal earlier revision of V.42.
This edge does not claim that LAPM is derived byte-for-byte from MNP.
This edge does not claim that every V.42 modem implemented every MNP class.
This edge does not equate MNP Class 5 compression with V.42bis compression.
open_questions: Acquire original Microcom MNP specifications and licensing records.
Extract the exact alternate-procedure/compatibility language from the November 1988 V.42 text.
Recover modem negotiation traces showing LAPM success and fallback to MNP.
Map which commercial modem models supported which MNP classes alongside which V.42 revisions.
notes: Canonical example of an installed proprietary/de-facto protocol surviving beside a newer formal standard through compatibility rather than formal revision.
